title: The Lost Trail
premise: Coral Crane, a railroad engineer haunted by a survey expedition that ended in a covered-up death, has spent years hopping between closed rail lines, repairing what the world abandoned. When his old rival Silas Vane hires Coral's crew to reopen a flooded mountain spur before monsoon season, Coral realizes the job is a trap: the line runs through the tunnel where his partner died, and Vane means to expose the truth Coral buried to save the crew. As the monsoon traps them with a leaking boat and dwindling supplies, Coral must choose between loyalty to the men who trusted him and the justice owed to a dead man's memory. In the end he confesses everything at the tunnel's mouth, letting the flood take the evidence—and his hiding place—with it.
about_author: Cyrus Pemberton is the pen name of a former railway surveyor who spent a decade mapping defunct lines across coastal ranges before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who live in the gaps between maps.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He repairs an abandoned trestle in the hills, establishing his itinerant life and the worn map of dead railroads he carries like a scar. A telegram arrives from Silas Vane offering work. Emotional beat: restless unease—the map is both refuge and prison.

chapters.title: The Crew That Stays Together
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. We meet his small loyal crew—Dess, Okonkwo, and young Pell—at a river camp, each drawn to Coral for reasons they don't fully say. The telegram burns unopened in his pocket. Beat: warmth shadowed by secrets.

chapters.title: An Offer With Teeth
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vane appears in person, charming and needling, offering triple pay to reopen the Kestrel Spur before monsoon. Coral refuses; Vane mentions the name 'Marrow,' Coral's dead partner. Beat: dread crystallizing into obligation.

chapters.title: Sworn Off
chapters.summary: Dess's POV. Dess confronts Coral about why he refused good money; Coral lies smoothly, and Dess pretends to believe him. Flashback fragments hint at a night ten years ago Coral never discusses. Beat: loyalty strained by silence.

chapters.title: Money Talks
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. The crew votes to take the job despite Coral's warning—winter debts are crushing them. Coral agrees to lead them rather than let them go unprotected. Beat: guilt disguised as duty.

chapters.title: Down the Flooded Line
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew travels the drowned valley toward Kestrel Spur by leaky boat, reading the ruined rails like scripture. Coral recognizes landmarks he swore he'd forgotten. Beat: memory rising like water.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. At a supply dock they take on a quiet stranger, Ilsa Reyes, who claims to be a hydrologist. Okonkwo doesn't trust her; she watches Coral too closely. Beat: suspicion entering the family.

chapters.title: Tunnel Mouth
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. They reach the sealed tunnel where Marrow died. Coral's hands shake as he surveys it; Vane's foremen are already there, too well-equipped, too expectant. Beat: the past made physical.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Questions
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. She probes Coral about the accident over camp coffee, revealing she knows details only an investigator—or Marrow's kin—would know. She is Marrow's daughter. Beat: truth knocking at the door.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Monsoon hits early, stranding everyone. Coral finds Vane's real plan: documents proving Coral falsified the original safety report to protect the company—and himself. Beat: betrayal and self-knowledge colliding.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Pell's POV. Attempting to run supplies upriver, Pell and Ilsa nearly drown when the boat splits; Ilsa saves Pell's life. The crew begins to trust her. Beat: fear forging unlikely bonds.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Dess's POV. Dess discovers Vane intends to pin Marrow's death entirely on Coral once the line reopens, clearing the company's name. Dess must decide whether to warn Coral or protect the crew's pay. Beat: loyalty versus survival.

chapters.title: Confession Interrupted
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral tries to tell Ilsa the truth about her father; Vane interrupts with a staged 'accident' that nearly kills Coral, framing it as equipment failure. Beat: terror that the truth may die with him.

chapters.title: Cut Off
chapters.summary: Okonkwo's POV. The flood washes out the return route; radio dead, food short. Vane's men grow desperate and dangerous. The crew realizes they're witnesses, not workers. Beat: claustrophobic dread.

chapters.title: Marrow's Notes
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa shares her father's letters, which reveal Marrow knew the tunnel was unstable and reported it—reports Coral never saw because Vane buried them. Coral's guilt shifts shape. Beat: grief reframed as revelation.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Culvert
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vane offers Coral escape by boat if he signs a confession taking sole blame. Coral asks for one night to decide. Beat: the seduction of a clean ending.

chapters.title: Night of Rising Water
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The river peaks; the camp floods; Vane's foremen try to seize the crew's evidence by force. Dess and Okonkwo fight them off in waist-deep water. Beat: chaos testing every bond.

chapters.title: Into the Tunnel
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral enters the half-flooded tunnel to retrieve Marrow's buried field notes—the physical proof Vane fears—with Ilsa covering his rope. Beat: courage born of reckoning.

chapters.title: Confrontation at Kestrel
chapters.summary: Climax, Coral's POV. Vane corners them at the tunnel mouth as the waters surge. Coral refuses the deal, reads Marrow's notes aloud over the storm, and lets the flood destroy the tunnel—and Vane's leverage—rather than bargain. Beat: truth chosen over survival.

chapters.title: After the Water
chapters.summary: Dess's POV. Dawn after the storm: Vane arrested when rescuers arrive, his forged ledger recovered from the mud. The crew counts itself lucky and changed. Beat: exhausted relief.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Plainly
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa and Coral hold a small memorial for Marrow at the tunnel's new mouth. Coral tells her the whole truth, unedited, and she chooses to stay and hear it through. Beat: mourning turned to grace.

chapters.title: The Open Line
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The crew rebuilds—not the spur, but a working ferry crossing the valley, choosing a life that stays put. Coral draws a new map, marking one line open. Beat: stillness earned at last.
